facts.statement: The species Albertonykus borealis was described by Nick Longrich and Phillip Currie in 2009.
facts.quote: The type species is A. borealis, described by Nick Longrich and Phillip Currie in 2009.

facts.statement: Albertonykus lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Upper Cretaceous in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Albertonykus (meaning "Alberta claw") is an extinct genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from the Maastrichtian-age (Upper Cretaceous) rocks of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: The site where Albertonykus fossils were found was originally discovered in 1910 by Barnum Brown while searching for Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1910, paleontologist Barnum Brown and his crew found a site filled with the bones of the gigantic tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus sarcophagus.

facts.statement: Over a dozen arm and leg bones of an unknown small theropod were excavated at the site in 2002 by a team led by Philip John Currie.
facts.quote: At the same site, over a dozen arm and leg bones belonging to an unknown species of small theropod were in 2002 excavated by a team of scientist led by Philip John Currie of the University of Alberta.

facts.statement: Nick Longrich identified the fossils as a new species in 2005 while comparing them to Albertosaurus claws.
facts.quote: In 2005 Nick Longrich, then a student at the University of Calgary, happened upon the small fossils while comparing Albertosaurus claws to other dinosaur species.

facts.statement: Albertonykus borealis lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Albertonykus borealis ( gr. "garra de Alberta del norte") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Albertonykus de dinosaurio terópodo alvarezsáurido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Albertonykus is the smallest known alvarezsaurid in North America, measuring 1.1 meters long and weighing 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Albertonykus is the smallest known alvarezsauridae ever discovered in North America, measuring 1.1 m long and weighing 5 kg.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Albertonykus preyed on wood-nesting termites based on evidence of borings in fossil wood from its habitat.
facts.quote: This leaves the possibility that Albertonykus preyed on wood-nesting termites.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis shows Albertonykus belongs to the Asian clade Mononykini, supporting the hypothesis that alvarezsaurs originated in South America and dispersed to Asia via North America.
facts.quote: After a phylogenetic analysis, it was shown that Albertonykus is a member of the Asian clade Mononykini, which supported the hypothesis that the alvarezsaurs originated in South America, and then dispersed to Asia through North America.

facts.statement: Albertonykus is the smallest alvarezsaurid found in North America, estimated at around 70 centimeters long, though other estimates place it at 1.1 meters long and 5 kg.
facts.quote: Albertonykus es el alvarezáurido más pequeño encontrado en Norteamérica, de alrededor de 70 centímetros de largo, aunque otras estimaciones lo colocan en el rango de los 1,1 metro de longitud y 5 kg de peso.

facts.statement: Albertonykus had a small, thin head, delicate neck, very long hind legs, and tiny arms dominated by a single finger, with other fingers being vestigial or absent.
facts.quote: Con una cabeza pequeña y fina, cuello delicado, patas traseras muy largas y brazos diminutos dominados por un único dedo, los otros dedos son vestigiales o no existen.

facts.statement: The robust arm structure of Albertonykus appears to be a specialization for excavating small holes to extract food.
facts.quote: Al parecer es una especialización para excava pequeños agujeros de los que extraer alimento.

facts.statement: Longrich and Currie found fossil wood with typical Termopsidae termite holes and galleries in the same formation where Albertonykus was found.
facts.quote: Longrich y Currie encontraron en la misma formación madera fósil con los típicos agujeros y galerías de las termitas Termopsidae.

facts.statement: Nick Longrich discovered the fossils in 2005 while comparing Albertosaurus claws with those of other dinosaur species.
facts.quote: En 2005 Nick Longrich, un paleontólogo en la Universidad de Calgary en Canadá encontró los fósiles mientras que comparaba garras de Albertosaurus con las de otras especies del dinosaurios

facts.statement: The fossils found in the Dry Island Bone Bed were dated to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Longrich después analizaba los fósiles encontrados en la cama de hueso de los Albertosaurus en Parque Provincial de Isla Dry que se dataron en 70 millones de años atrás

facts.statement: Although fragments of the Albertonykus skeleton had been discovered before, they were never identified as a separate species.
facts.quote: Aunque los fragmentos del esqueleto de Albertonykus hubieran sido descubiertos antes, nunca habían sido identificados como una especie separada.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis shows that Albertonykus is a sister taxon to the Asian clade Mononykinae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético demuestra que Albertonykus es un taxón hermano del clado asiático Mononykinae

facts.statement: The discovery of Albertonykus provides important data on the biology of Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Albertonykus proporciona datos importantes en la biología de Alvarezsauridae.

facts.statement: It is one of the few Alvarezsauridae remains found outside of South America or Asia.
facts.quote: Es uno de los pocos restos de alvarezsáuridos encontrado fuera de Sudamérica o Asia.

facts.statement: Albertonykus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Albertonykus belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Alvarezsauridae

facts.statement: Albertonykus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
